idea-plugin.name: Web Frontend Mini
idea-plugin.description:
Web Frontend Mini brings the web frontend stack to OpenIDE: syntax highlighting, code formatting, CSS Modules intelligence and Catppuccin color schemes for the files the IDE opens as plain text — .css .scss .less .js .ts .vue and friends. Pure Java; the built-in features need no Node.js and pair perfectly with LSP servers via LSP4IJ when you want more.

What you get

  • Syntax highlighting for css scss less js mjs cjs ts tsx jsx vue via TextMate grammars (MIT sources); in .vue the template, <script> and <style> are all colored.
  • Code formatting — Reformat (Ctrl+Alt+L) and format-on-save: nesting indentation for braces and <tag> pairs everywhere (incl. vue templates), line & spacing rules ({ } ; , :) for the CSS family; indent-on-Enter and Ctrl+/ comments with the syntax of the region.
  • CSS Modules in .vue: completion for $style.*, named modules (<style module="named">) and classes imported from *.module.css; Ctrl+B jumps to the class definition (inline block or external file).
  • Navigation: Ctrl+B on <style|script src="./file"> paths in .vue opens the file.
  • 4 color schemes «Catppuccin Mocha / Macchiato / Frappe / Latte + Web» with all web-stack and LSP semantic-token keys baked in.
  • Spellchecking that doesn't stumble over tag contents; grammar-based code folding.

Good to know

  • Formatting defaults: Settings → Editor → Code Style → TextMate (2 spaces; one shared profile for all web file types — platform limitation).
  • PHP / Blade / Twig / Smarty are served by the separate PHP for OpenIDE plugin, HTML by the platform — this plugin deliberately doesn't touch them.
  • Richer hover/completion comes from LSP servers (Volar, typescript-language-server, vscode-css-languageserver) connected via LSP4IJ; the plugin's own features work without any LSP.

Clean-room replacement for the license-gated web-tools plugin. Sources and setup guide: GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• v1.15.3: vue/css Reformat was silently stolen by LSP4IJ — its LSPFormattingOnlyService grabs any file with an attached formatting-capable language server (Volar on .vue, css-ls on .css) and wins the FormattingService selection. Our service now sorts explicitly BEFORE both LSP4IJ formatting services (the before-rules are no-ops when LSP4IJ is absent). The formatting task also logs its start and catches all throwables, so idea.log always shows how far a Reformat went.
  • v1.15.2: "Reformat does nothing" for css/js/ts/vue root-caused and fixed: ReformatCodeAction.update() disables the action when no lang.formatter resolves for the file's language — v1.15.0 removed the registration, so Ctrl+Alt+L never reached the Prettier service at all (blade kept working only because the PHP plugin registers its own builder). A no-op dummy builder re-enables the action; the external service still does the real formatting.
  • v1.15.1: formatting-service feature fix — whole-file Reformat (Ctrl+Alt+L / Actions on Save) requires AD_HOC_FORMATTING to consult the service at all, which css files were silently missing; global tool discovery is now version-independent (every nvm version's lib/node_modules is scanned, each tool runs with the node of its own version — switching or adding node versions no longer breaks formatting); global prettier also receives --stdin-filepath for correct parser resolution; canFormat negatives are logged.
  • v1.15.0: formatting now delegates to real formatters — Prettier (css/scss/less/js/ts/jsx/vue; the project's own .prettierrc is honored, prettier is resolved from the project node_modules or the npm global root) and blade-formatter (.blade.php). The built-in lexeme formatter is retired: its block model also fed the platform's startup indent auto-adjust, which kept re-indenting files on every open. Requirements: Node.js on the machine (nvm layout discovered automatically; override via the wfm.node.path / wfm.npm.global.root VM options). When no tool is found, Reformat is a safe no-op.
  • v1.14.0: the two real "formatter does nothing / every press adds indent" root-causes, found by reading the platform engine sources (262) and an offline engine lab (./build.sh test now runs the real FormatProcessor against the plugin's block model — idempotency + fuzzer): (1) edits died silently in PsiBasedFormattingModel — the TextMate PSI is parsed with an EmptyLexer and has no WHITE_SPACE nodes, so every whitespace replacement no-oped; the model now applies edits directly to the Document (DocumentBasedFormattingModel); (2) the indent-options AUTO-DETECTOR ran on every Reformat and, on mixed tabs/spaces files, detected different options each time — the indentation drifted forever; a fileIndentOptionsProvider now pins the options to the TextMate Code Style profile (Settings → Editor → Code Style → TextMate). Reformat is idempotent and converges.
  • v1.13.2: THE "reformat changes nothing" root-cause: the root block reported itself as a leaf (isLeaf was !composite), so the engine never descended into children and produced zero edits for any file — while models were still built (the indent detector walks getSubBlocks directly, masking it in logs). A leaf is now a single-lexeme block. Reformat should finally apply to css/scss/less/js/ts/vue/blade.
  • v1.13.1: fixed v1.13.0 regressions — the code-style provider crashed settings init (getRootSettings is @NotNull during defaults construction; the indent auto-detection experiment is reverted) causing 77 errors and a broken file tree on startup, and two .tmPreferences files carried a mistyped closing tag which broke bundle registration. build.sh now validates every bundled XML/JSON at build time.
  • v1.13.0: Blade (.blade.php) gets Reformat — the same lexeme formatter registered for the Blade language via a new minimal bundled grammar (tags + {{ }} echoes; @directive bodies are not re-indented yet). CSS: indent auto-detection disabled for TextMate (mixed tabs/spaces sources made every Ctrl+Alt+L re-detect a different style — looked like ever-growing indents; the formatter itself is idempotent).
  • v1.12.1: fixed a platform error — the formatter class requested the Formatter service from its static initializer (Spacing presets); the presets now load lazily on first real formatting. CSS spacing: commas and colons no longer collapse multi-line selector/value lists (typed line breaks survive). Model builds are logged at INFO to diagnose per-file formatting.
  • v1.12.0: the real OutOfMemory root-cause, found by token fuzzing: a single-lexeme leaf block produced a child identical to itself (same range), so walkers like the startup indent auto-detector built infinite leaf-to-leaf chains — millions of blocks. Single-lexeme blocks now never have children; verified against 20,000 fuzzed token sequences (worst case linear). The earlier v1.11.1/v1.11.2 fixes were correct but partial and are kept.
  • v1.11.2: startup/typing memory storm fixed — the indent auto-detector requests a formatting model per line; each request re-lexed the whole document before, overloading the GC (cascading OOMs). Models are now cached per file (invalidated on document change); oversized/no-grammar files get a no-op dummy model; createModel call rate is logged.
  • v1.11.1: critical fix — Reformat (Ctrl+Alt+L) froze the IDE with OutOfMemory: a formatting group was re-detected as its own child, producing an infinite single-child block chain (7.4M blocks / 1.2GB in the heap dump). Install this version before using Reformat.
  • v1.11.0: Reformat aligns vue template tag nesting (tag blocks in the formatter); marketplace-style description with change-notes.
  • v1.10.0: own code formatter (Reformat, format-on-save, indent-on-Enter, Ctrl+/ comments via bundled .tmPreferences), Code Style page for TextMate, CSS Modules completion and Ctrl+B navigation in .vue.
  • v1.9.1: Ctrl+B navigation for external <style>/<script> src files in .vue.
  • v1.9.0: vue script/style finally colored (embedded-scope mechanics).
  • v1.8.x: spellchecking, self-contained «+ Web» schemes, whole-document re-lex fix, bundle layout fix.
